content:
If you're a heavy Apple Watch user who participated in testing this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

The related updates will be pushed via the App Store, with the update notes reading: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27, and does not include any new features."

Apple notified developers this week that the related update process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates have been pushed out with ample time.

Apple stated that because some watchOS apps had issues with parts of their arm64 architecture, this measure needed to be taken. They appear to be automatically reprocessing and repackaging the apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without developers having to take any action.
